primary.title: Experiments in Plant Hybridization
primary.author: Gregor Mendel
primary.rationale: Mendel's seminal paper detailing his experiments with pea plants and the foundational principles of heredity. This is his most important published work.

secondary.title: Gregor Mendel: A Life
secondary.author: Daniel L. Hartl
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive biography of Gregor Mendel by a prominent geneticist, offering insights into his life, work, and the scientific context of his discoveries.

secondary.title: The Monk and the Riddle: Life and Science of Gregor Mendel
secondary.author: C. D. Darlington
secondary.rationale: While slightly before the 1976 cutoff, this is a highly regarded and detailed account of Mendel's life and scientific contributions, often cited in later scholarship. It provides significant historical context.

secondary.title: Gregor Mendel's 'Experiments in Plant Hybridization'
secondary.author: R. A. Fisher
secondary.rationale: Although published before 1976, Fisher's statistical analysis of Mendel's data is a landmark secondary source that significantly influenced the modern interpretation of Mendel's work and is essential for understanding the reception of his findings.

suggestions.notes: Primary source availability is high for Mendel's key publication. Secondary sources are abundant, with a focus on scholarly biographies and analyses of his work. The inclusion of Fisher's 1936 article is justified due to its profound and lasting impact on Mendel scholarship, even though it predates the 1976 cutoff.
